text: Run the per-pixel net on matrix hardware via cooperative vectors (VK_NV_cooperative_vector / a KHR successor) where the driver offers it
description: Our net is exactly the case cooperative vectors target: every fragment evaluates its own small MLP (132→32→16→8), weights loaded on demand from a buffer. Today it runs as fp16 packed FMAs (experiments c30bda7, 6.3 ms on Vega at 700 MHz). Check: which Vulkan drivers (RADV, Turnip/Adreno 750 on the Frame, NVIDIA desktop) expose cooperative vectors or cooperative matrix in 2026; if any do, add a variant of net.frag behind a feature check, keeping the fp16 path as fallback. Sources: docs.vulkan.org VK_NV_cooperative_vector proposal; NVIDIA neural-shading blog.

status.comment: Local: Mesa 26.2.4 RADV on Renoir exposes neither cooperative matrix nor vector; shaderFloat16 = true, fp16 path is right here. Research 2026-11-23: Mesa release notes 25.2-26.1 list VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix for RADV (RDNA3+), NVK (Turing+), ANV; none for Turnip. Vulkan 1.4.359 (Aug 2026) added VK_EXT_cooperative_matrix_maintenance1 with Qualcomm among contributors, so Adreno support may come via Qualcomm's proprietary driver first. Human step (needs the Steam Frame): run `vulkaninfo | grep -i -E 'cooperative|float16'` on the Frame (or from adb/ssh shell on it) and paste the output. If neither extension is listed, cancel this idea; fp16 stays. Sources: docs.mesa3d.org/relnotes/25.2.0, 26.1.0; phoronix.com/news/Vulkan-1.4.359
